dammed_river.notes: Not established in any source retrieved on 2026-09-03; dammed_river was previously recorded as false with that caveat in notes. Null until a fetched source states it either way.

fall_height_m.notes: Francese et al. (2025) state the path 'extended from 3213 to 2300 m a.s.l.' and that the avalanche ended 'at an elevation of 2330 m a.s.l.'; the vertical drop is not stated as a figure and is not computed here.

rock_fraction.notes: A pure ice (glacieret) failure per Francese et al. (2025); no rock fraction stated.

secondary_surge.notes: Not established in any source retrieved on 2026-09-03; secondary_surge was previously recorded as false with that caveat in notes. Null until a fetched source states it either way.

seismic.notes: Francese et al. (2025): 'An earthquake triggering the failure was excluded based on the processing of the available seismological observations'; no seismic signal of the collapse itself was read.

name: Marmolada glacier (Punta Rocca glacieret) collapse, Dolomites, Italy
notes: Small-volume, high-consequence ice avalanche. Olivieri et al. (2022, Remote Sensing Letters) was Crossref-resolved but its landing page is behind a bot challenge, so it is not cited.

peak_velocity_ms.notes: 'The avalanche reached a maximum speed of 80–90 km h−1', converted to m/s

precursors_observed.description: Francese et al. (2025): unusually high air temperatures 'led to an excess of meltwater, which, since mid-June, had overpressurized the englacial discharge network'; at collapse 'crevasses were completely water-filled'. No lead time is stated as such.

runout_km.notes: 'traveled for approximately 2.3 km along the northern slope'

estimates.qualifier: 'occurred at an altitude of approximately 3200 m'
figure caption: flow path 'extended from 3213 to 2300 m a.s.l.'

source_location.basis: Marmolada Glacier coordinates 46°26′32″ N, 11°51′53″ E stated by Francese et al. (2025), converted to decimal degrees; the failed glacieret lies 'in a small cirque just below Punta Rocca (3309 m a.s.l.)'

source_volume_m3.notes: 'The detached ice mass had an estimated volume of 70 400 m3'

sources.excerpt: The detached ice mass had an estimated volume of 70 400 m 3 and slid down the slope, killing 11 mountaineers after having traveled for approximately 2.3 km along the northern slope.
sources.title: Failure of Marmolada Glacier (Dolomites, Italy) in 2022: data-based back analysis of possible collapse mechanisms

time.basis: 'The collapse in the early afternoon of 3 July 2022' (Francese et al. 2025); no clock time was read, so the instant is 14:00 CEST (UTC+2) with a two-hour uncertainty
